content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":4,"description_fidelity":6,"readability_1x":5,"pixel_craft":5,"palette_discipline":4,"appeal":6},"score":51,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["At 1x the silhouette reads more like a tiny fish or eyeball with a striped tail than a squid with gathering and thrusting tentacles.","The oversized circular head and two large square eye sockets use a modern mascot-like construction rather than the compact mechanical forms typical of Mega Man 2-3 enemies.","Detached or weakly connected black pixels above the rear edge and below the right appendage look like accidental fragments.","The lower outline is excessively heavy, forming a large black mass that obscures the body and tentacle separation.","The trailing appendages merge into one horizontally striped wedge instead of distinct tentacle clusters capable of showing a pulse animation.","The sprite uses too many blue and violet ramps within small tile areas; the layered band shading is not disciplined like an NES three-color sprite palette.","There is no visible red-eye warning state or mine-like mechanical detail to communicate its proximity trigger and explosive role."],"fixes":["Reduce the head to a simpler 12-14 px mechanical dome with a consistent one-pixel black contour.","Replace the striped rear wedge with three or four clearly separated tentacles, using one gathered frame and one splayed thrust frame.","Remove the detached black pixels above the rear and beneath the right side; connect necessary extremities with deliberate one-pixel joints.","Thin the bottom outline and carve background notches between tentacles so the silhouette remains readable at 1x.","Limit each 8x8 region to black plus two blues and one light cyan or white; remove the extra violet and intermediate blue bands.","Make the eyes smaller and more robotic, then reserve a red palette swap or red eye pixels for the warning frame.","Add one compact mine cue, such as a central seam, rivet, or small fuse-like sensor, without increasing the color count."]}
